rulings.challenge_claim: The find-root that the adjoining span (p02-026) makes its whole binding device is already attested inside this row's own span at oshb:Eccl.7.24 and is never named; the K/Q verse (oshb:Eccl.7.22) used as this row's opening seam evidence is cited without its inline-ketiv disclosure.
rulings.grounds: Root-sweep independently re-derived: sweep.py --skel over the bare matsa root (contiguous consonantal substring, skeleton tier) returns 11 verses / 15 tokens book-wide, undercounting the plene-spelled participle וּמוֹצֶ֨א at oshb:Eccl.7.26 and the plene infinitive לִמְצוֹא֙ at oshb:Eccl.8.17 (both escape the substring search because an infixed vav breaks the contiguous run). Adding those two byte-tier tokens gives 12 verses / 17 tokens book-wide, matching OL's digit exactly. oshb:Eccl.7.24, inside THIS row's own span, carries יִמְצָאֶֽנּוּ (byte tier) -- a matsa-root token one verse before the seam the next row uses as its whole binding device -- and the row discloses that verse only for its paseq mark and general search vocabulary, never naming the root. Per the cross-seam cohesion rule, a byte-true device straddling the row's own seam argues continuity against the row unless disclosed. An unused byte-true catchword is also present: oshb:Eccl.7.23 closes on רְחוֹקָ֥ה and oshb:Eccl.7.24 opens on רָח֖וֹק (same root, byte tier) -- stronger cohesion evidence than the tier-3 paseq the row does cite. Secondary point, confirmed: web:Eccl.7.22, cited as this row's backward-seam evidence, is one of the 12 K/Q verses in pmarks_Eccl.json; its byte text reads (in sequence) אֲשֶׁ֥ר גַּם את אַתָּ֖ה -- the unpointed ketiv (את) sitting inline beside the pointed qere (אַתָּ֖ה), undisclosed. This second point is weaker (the row never quotes or slices oshb:Eccl.7.22, only cites the ref categorically) and does not on its own carry the ruling; the matsa-root cross-seam finding is sufficient alone.
rulings.remedy: Add one device_notes sentence naming the matsa-root token at oshb:Eccl.7.24 as texture straddling this row's own closing seam (cross-seam cohesion disclosure), and disclose the K/Q status of oshb:Eccl.7.22 if it continues to be cited as boundary evidence. Test the cure must pass: the row's device_notes must name the object (matsa root) per SEMANTIC-CLASS COUNT DISCIPLINE, and a K/Q disclosure sweep over the row's cited refs must show zero undisclosed K/Q sites.

rulings.challenge_claim: The six-token find-root arithmetic and the feminine frame verb are byte-true, but the five perfect tokens are cited under one pointed byte form attested only three times, and the comparison to the book's other two frame intrusions misdescribes what varies.
rulings.grounds: Root arithmetic re-verified from bytes: oshb:Eccl.7.27 carries מָצָ֔אתִי and לִמְצֹ֥א; oshb:Eccl.7.28 carries three tokens -- מָצָ֑אתִי, מָצָ֔אתִי, מָצָֽאתִי; oshb:Eccl.7.29 carries מָצָ֔אתִי -- 6 tokens over 3 verses, confirming the row's own count (5 perfect + 1 infinitive) is correct. But the row quotes ONE exact pointed form (מָצָ֔אתִי, zaqef qaton) as representing 'five' perfect occurrences; re-collated at byte tier that exact form matches only 3 verses / 3 tokens (oshb:Eccl.7.27, the middle token of oshb:Eccl.7.28, and oshb:Eccl.7.29) -- the other two tokens at oshb:Eccl.7.28 (מָצָ֑אתִי with atnach, מָצָֽאתִי with silluq/meteg) are different byte forms. Citing a skeleton/root-level count of five under a single byte-tier quoted form is a TIER/ORDINAL DISCIPLINE violation. Second, oshb:Eccl.1.2 reads אָמַ֣ר קֹהֶ֔לֶת and oshb:Eccl.12.8 reads אָמַ֥ר הַקּוֹהֶ֖לֶת -- the SAME masculine perfect verb (אָמַ֣ר = אָמַ֥ר) at both sites, byte-identical; only the qohelet-noun spelling (plene definite at 12:8) differs. The row's claim that the book's other two amar-qohelet sites 'use different forms again' overstates variation that is not in the verb.
rulings.remedy: Re-cut the tier label: either name the 'five' count as a skeleton/root-level object ("5 perfect-tense matsa tokens, skeleton tier, oshb:Eccl.7.27-7.29") rather than attaching it to one quoted byte form, or quote each of the three distinct byte forms at oshb:Eccl.7.28 individually if a byte-tier claim is kept. Correct the comparison sentence: the verb אָמַ֣ר is identical at 1:2 and 12:8; only the qohelet-noun spelling varies. Test: re-collate the cited form against verse_map_oshb.json -- the byte-tier hit count must equal the verse/token count the prose claims for that tier.

rulings.challenge_claim: The row argues only its forward boundary (8:1 vs 8:2) and is silent on its own backward boundary against 7:29, leaving an unused mi-construction warrant (7:24/8:1 interrogative-of-cognition echo) undisclosed.
rulings.grounds: Confirmed from the row's own fields: boundary_evidence_refs = [web:Eccl.8.1, web:Eccl.8.2] only; boundary_rationale and strongest_rejected_alternative never mention web:Eccl.7.29 or engage why 8:1 is not folded into the preceding span. Candidate warrant verified byte-true: oshb:Eccl.7.24 closes on מִ֥י יִמְצָאֶֽנּוּ ('who can find it out') and oshb:Eccl.8.1 opens on מִ֚י כְּהֶ֣חָכָ֔ם וּמִ֥י יוֹדֵ֖עַ ('who is like the wise, and who knows') -- both open on the same interrogative (מִ֚י / וּמִ֥י) plus a verb of knowing/finding, an interrogative-of-cognition construction bracketing the 7:23-8:1 quest material from both ends, byte-verified and left uncited on this row's backward side. DISTINCT from the OL challenge on this same row (see next ruling): this defect is about the row's silence on its BACKWARD seam via an unused mi-interrogative construction; OL's is about an unsupported claim on the row's FORWARD seam via an undisclosed davar-root chain. Different devices, different directions -- not the same defect.
rulings.remedy: Add a sentence to boundary_rationale (or a boundary_evidence_refs entry for web:Eccl.7.29) disclosing the mi-interrogative echo as cross-seam texture and stating why the register shift (rhetorical proem vs. the search testimony's perfect-tense frame) still argues for separateness. rulings.challenge_claim: The row rests entirely on a negative lexical claim against 8:2 ('shares no content token'), while a byte-true davar-family chain runs one token through each of oshb:Eccl.8.1-8.5 across that seam, undisclosed and untested by any sweep.
rulings.grounds: Word-bound davar-family token confirmed in each of five consecutive verses (byte tier, verse_map_oshb.json): דָּבָ֑ר (oshb:Eccl.8.1), דִּבְרַ֖ת (oshb:Eccl.8.2), בְּדָבָ֣ר רָ֑ע (oshb:Eccl.8.3), דְּבַר (oshb:Eccl.8.4), דָּבָ֣ר רָ֑ע (oshb:Eccl.8.5). The row's claim that its verse 'shares no content token' with web:Eccl.8.2 survives only at the attested-spelling level (דָּבָ֑ר vs דִּבְרַ֖ת are different inflected spellings); at root level the two verses head a five-verse chain, and this book's hazard catalog names exactly this trap (attested-spelling vs. root sweeps return different digits). The row cites no digit and quotes no Hebrew at all from oshb:Eccl.8.2, the verse it is contrasting against. DISTINCT from the LF challenge on this row (backward-seam silence via the mi-interrogative construction) -- this is a forward-seam, unsupported-negative-claim defect.
rulings.remedy: Either run and cite a root-level davar-family sweep across oshb:Eccl.8.1-8.5 and disclose the chain as cross-seam texture, or narrow the claim to 'no shared token at the attested-spelling level' rather than the unqualified 'no content token.' Test: citation_sweep.py / check_universals.py should show the claim carrying an adjacent digit-bearing sweep citation naming the swept object (spelling vs. root).

rulings.challenge_claim: The opening first-person reading depends on a verb the WEB rendering supplies and the Hebrew does not carry; the curly-quoted WEB fragment attached to that claim is mismatched; the behal/bahel stem contrast is under-quoted (only one side's Hebrew shown); and the only two-verse davar-ra collocation in the book brackets this row's own closing seam undisclosed.
rulings.grounds: oshb:Eccl.8.2 opens on the bare pronoun אֲנִי֙ with no verb of speaking anywhere in the verse (byte tier). WEB's full rendering is: "I say, 'Keep the king's command!' because of the oath to God" -- 'I say' is supplied by the translation, not carried by the Hebrew bytes, and the crux (a first-person pronoun governing an imperative, שְׁמ֔וֹר, with no intervening verb) goes unnamed. The row's curly-quoted fragment “because of the oath to God” (web:Eccl.8.2) is confirmed to be the verse's CLOSING oath clause, not the opening self-address the row attaches it to -- a quote/claim mismatch. The stem contrast (niphal תִּבָּהֵ֤ל at oshb:Eccl.8.3 vs. piel תְּבַהֵ֨ל at oshb:Eccl.5.1=web:Eccl.5.2) is plausible from the pointed bytes -- the two forms are visibly distinct at byte tier -- but the row never quotes oshb:Eccl.5.1's Hebrew anywhere, leaving one side of its own claim unshown, in a book whose staged extract carries no morphology layer to verify it independently. Confirmed by sweep.py --skel over the davar-ra collocation (skeleton tier): בְּדָבָ֣ר רָ֑ע / דָּבָ֣ר רָ֑ע occurs in exactly 2 verses book-wide (oshb:Eccl.8.3, oshb:Eccl.8.5), bracketing this row's own closing seam (8:4|8:5), undisclosed on this side.
rulings.remedy: Re-cut boundary_rationale so the curly-quoted WEB fragment matches the claim it supports (quote the actual self-address portion or drop the mismatched fragment) and disclose the pronoun+imperative crux rather than treating it as settled. Quote oshb:Eccl.5.1's Hebrew alongside the existing 8:3 quote before asserting the niphal/piel contrast, or soften to a texture note pending morphological confirmation outside the staged tools. Add a device_notes sentence disclosing the davar-ra collocation at 8:3/8:5 as cross-seam texture. Test: check_web_quotes.py should confirm the curly-quoted WEB fragment sits adjacent to the claim it actually supports; citation_sweep.py should show the collocation disclosed per the cross-seam cohesion rule.

rulings.challenge_claim: The row's stated binding evidence is a verbatim recurrence the bytes refute -- the pointed form it says stands at both 8:5 and 8:6 is attested at only one of them, at every tier.
rulings.grounds: Independently re-derived via sweep.py --skel over the vav-prefixed et-umishpat phrase (byte tier): returns EXACTLY 1 verse, oshb:Eccl.8.5. oshb:Eccl.8.6 reads עֵ֣ת וּמִשְׁפָּ֑ט -- NO vav prefix (verse_map_oshb.json, byte tier) -- against oshb:Eccl.8.5's וְעֵ֣ת וּמִשְׁפָּ֔ט, and the two forms also differ at the terminal accent (zaqef qaton at 8:5 vs. atnach at 8:6). The row's device_notes explicitly states וְעֵ֣ת וּמִשְׁפָּ֔ט stands at oshb:Eccl.8.5 'and again at oshb:Eccl.8.6' -- byte-false at every tier (byte, accent_stripped, and skeleton alike, since even skeleton tier requires the vav to match this exact phrase). sweep.py --skel over the same phrase WITHOUT the vav confirms a genuine 2-verse skeleton-tier collocation (oshb:Eccl.8.5, oshb:Eccl.8.6) -- a real and sufficient cohesion signal, but a DIFFERENT object at a DIFFERENT tier than the byte-tier 'verbatim' claim the row's whole cohesion argument for this five-verse span rests on. This is exactly the defect class the book's tier discipline names: 'byte-identical/verbatim' asserted without the correct tier.
rulings.remedy: Correct boundary_rationale and device_notes to state the et-umishpat collocation recurs at SKELETON tier across oshb:Eccl.8.5-8.6 (not byte-tier 'verbatim'), dropping the false vav-inclusive framing; the underlying cohesion argument for holding 8:5-8:9 together survives (the skeleton-tier 2-verse collocation is real) but must be re-cut to the correct tier -- this is the test the replacement warrant must pass. Test: collate.py --ref oshb:Eccl.8.6 --quote (the vav-prefixed form וְעֵ֣ת וּמִשְׁפָּ֔ט, as the row currently quotes it) must return no byte-tier match -- the cure passes when the row's own re-collation matches the tier it claims.
